source.title: Gradients Look Alike: Sensitivity is Often Overestimated in DP-SGD
source.authors: Anvith Thudi; Hengrui Jia; Casey Meehan; Ilia Shumailov; Nicolas Papernot

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper, including appendices. Some figure text is garbled, but the relevant result descriptions are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests per-instance differential privacy guarantees for DP-SGD, not the catalog claim about memorization capacity, natural-label test error, or train–test generalization gaps. It discusses generalization and memorization as implications of privacy guarantees.
record.gate_note: The paper reports privacy-bound results and classification correctness as a condition associated with privacy bounds. It does not measure the train–test generalization gap, and the accuracy relation is not itself a result about that gap.
record.test_reason: The study derives and estimates per-instance privacy upper bounds for DP-SGD. Sections 4 and Appendix B compare these bounds across training stages, classification correctness, architectures and batch sizes, without measuring any version's specified generalization effect. Discussion of memorization and generalization supplies implications, not tests of V1–V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that their analysis certifies tighter per-instance DP guarantees for many benchmark datapoints, explaining limits on privacy attacks under the specified neighboring-dataset threat model. Correctness-associated privacy differences are observed; generalization and memorization are discussed as implications. Computing the guarantees remains expensive.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains DP-SGD models and analyzes per-instance privacy leakage; it does not use the generalization-gap measurements or interventions in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported privacy bounds vary with training stage, update rule, minibatch size, DP strength, architecture, and whether datapoints are classified correctly. These are changes in privacy bounds, not measured generalization gaps.

fits_no_version.finding: On MNIST and CIFAR-10, the analysis gives many datapoints tighter per-instance privacy upper bounds than the classical data-independent guarantee, especially later in training (Section 4.1).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Data-dependent analysis can certify stronger per-instance privacy for many datapoints under DP-SGD.

fits_no_version.finding: Correctly classified datapoints have better per-step privacy bounds on average than incorrectly classified datapoints, with the strongest disparity late in training (Section 4.1, Figure 3; Appendix B, Figure 22).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Classification correctness is associated with stronger per-instance privacy guarantees under the studied DP-SGD settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing expected minibatch size lowers the estimated privacy bound for the mean update rule, whereas the sum update rule's bound generally increases (Section 4.2; Appendix B). These outcomes are privacy bounds rather than held-out error.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The relationship between minibatch size and per-instance privacy bounds depends on the update rule.

record.problems: The experiments estimate privacy guarantees rather than generalization. The authors note computational limitations, including repeated training runs and expensive expectation estimates. Several findings are presented in figures; numerical values for many plotted distributions are not available in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No rows: reported outcomes concern per-instance privacy bounds, not a version's named behavior or measure. Privacy-bound results are therefore not catalog rows for these claim versions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting capacity and held-out accuracy under natural versus random labels.
Held-out error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected held-out performance and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout's effect on held-out error across training-set sizes and regularization settings.
Magnitude-aware sharpness ranking generalization gaps against norm- and margin-based measures.
Test-accuracy loss after removing highly memorized examples compared with removing random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Correct the record's relation from tests to discusses; T6 and the empty result-row and verdict lists are appropriate. Privacy bounds do not establish random-label memorization capacity, train–test gaps, or the test-accuracy effect of removing memorized examples. The cited memorization literature does not supply this study's own V8 results.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out accuracy on natural versus random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond interpolation.
Generalization differences among adaptive and non-adaptive optimizers.
Test performance under varying batch sizes and epoch budgets.
Sharpness or other measured properties tracking train–test generalization gaps.
Effect on test accuracy of removing memorized examples.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
